reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.2): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Both reviewers re-read every German string in the fixed unit: the Folge, the three LS inputs (lines, web page, LS3 board), the 11 LS4 texts, the redemittel, the three rule cards the unit shows (a1.2/rule-cards.json: rc.temporal-praepositionen, rc.ordinalzahlen-datum, rc.imperativ-sie), the Sp2 and S1 Aufgaben, the story, the Fokus, the facts and every explanation.de. They solved every item blind, from promptDe plus options, tiles or the played line only: the gist item, 15 input items, 12 structured items, 36 pool items, 15 reserve items, 4 perception items, 11 exam items, 9 check items and 4 proof items. Questionable answers were run through the real checker (src/lib/lesson/check.js, via checkAnswer + checkOptionsFor): Reisepass, Fotokopie, 0176 2345 67, 0176-234567, 16 Uhr 30 and the ls3-p10 midfield order. The player's perception path was re-read: ItemView.jsx l. 105–116 plays speak || quoteOf(promptDe) and masks the quote until the item is answered. The exam blocks were checked against registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1, h3, sp2, s1), and all 11 exam texts and the S1 situation were recounted. The grammar ceiling was checked against grammar-spine.json and a1-2.md §6 unit 4 and §9. Can-dos were checked against registries/cando/a1.json; cast facts against casts/a1.json and casts/series.json; the plan against a1-2.md §5, §6, §8 and §11. Every weekday–date pair was recomputed for 2026, the year in which 1 June is a Monday. Each of the 32 round-1 findings was verified against the current file (see previousRound).

verdict: Not exit-ready, but close. The count is 1 BLOCKER (validator EXM-02), 2 MAJOR and 12 MINOR, with a total of 25/35 (round 1: 21). Round 2 confirms 24 of the 32 round-1 findings as fixed. 4 are partly fixed (F23, F26, F28, F32) and 4 are open (F15, F27, F31, and the fokusPlan follow-up of F29). What stops exit: (1) the H1 block is now pictorial but its six images are only „planned“, and a .2 course cannot run it. The fix that also restores the plan is sd1.l3 in its place (F01). (2) The ordinal rule card still generates ✗„achtte“ (F02, the round-1 F15, not fixed). (3) Reisepass and Fotokopie are rejected in two reserve items (F03). Everything else is minor. Two H3 stems are loose, and there are accepted-form inconsistencies, lexicon roles, three continuity nits, the plan/Fokus spec drift and tooling gate holes. After F01–F03 and at most five of the minors, a round 3 should reach 0/0 with every criterion ≥ 4.

scoreRationale.D: 3. The inputs, exam texts and Aufgaben are correct and idiomatic after the round-1 fixes. But the level's ordinal rule card still states a rule that produces ✗„achtte“ (F02, major), and several explanations cite words without quotation marks (F11).
scoreRationale.N: 4. The lexis, sentence length and grammar are on level, and Konjunktiv II is back to the planned chunk. The small role mismatches (receptive Kopie typed; months receptive but produced, F06) are the only look-ahead signal.
scoreRationale.H: 4. The scenes are believable and lively, and every can-do is now performed, the title can-do in the Sp2 phone call. One proof is still recognition-only (F12).
scoreRationale.A: 3. Every key is correct and determined by the German prompt. But two defensible full forms are rejected (Reisepass, Fotokopie: F03, major), two H3 stems are loose (F04), and ls3-p10 and the number formats accept inconsistently (F05, F13).
scoreRationale.P: 3. H3, S1 and Sp2 match sd1.json in items, options, plays, word bands, register and rubric. But the H1 block cannot run in a .2 course without approved images (F01, validator blocker), and the plan's Lesen Teile are still missing with no deviation record (F09).
scoreRationale.K: 4. The facts are verified and current, the Meldepflicht timeline is now part of the story, and the building, calendar and cast are consistent. Small breaks: the LS2 voice is the absent clerk (F07), Bilal's flat and the „Antrag“ (F08), one reserve weekday (F10), and „die U2“ in Leipzig on the shown card (F14).
scoreRationale.E: 4. Instructions are ≤ 90 characters, pools and steps are standard size, and each endLine names a win the step delivers. LS4 (11 double-played texts) is the longest step but stays within its 20 minutes.

findings.quote: validate.mjs EXM-02: „sd1.h1 is pictorial and the block has no approved image assets; in a1.2 that blocks the lane (§4.9)“ · all six assets: "status": "planned"

It follows from the round-1 fix for F23. sd1.h1 is now pictorial:true, and t6–t11 point to assets a01–a06, but all six assets are still „planned“. A .2 course may never run the text variant (BLUEPRINT §4.9, §10 LS5 note), so the H1 block cannot go live and the unit cannot exit. H1 was never planned for this unit. a1-2.md §5 row 4, §6 unit 4 and the §11 matrix give u04 L2, L3, H3, S1 and Sp2, and they put H1 in units 1, 6, 7, 10 and 12. The alt texts and prompts themselves are sound: each matches its item's options in order, and no image shows a real document or brand.
findings.fix: Preferred: replace the H1 block with the plan's sd1.l3, which is non-pictorial. Use 5 Schilder or Aushänge in and around the Bürgerbüro, one richtig/falsch statement each, 10–25 words per sign. Take the situations from the LS3 board and the LS1 page, but do not copy their sentences, so the items are not ITM-04 copies. Then update spec.lanes.pruefungsfokus and start.pruefungsfokusChips, both in the unit and in specs.json, and swap the h1 strategy card for an l3 card. Keep t6–t11 and a01–a06 for an H1 unit of the plan (6, 7 or 10). This also closes F09. Alternative: run the image pipeline for a01–a06 and get the owner's batch approval (status "approved", D16). Until then, the unit stays blocked.

findings.quote: „Bis 19: Zahl + -te: der zweite, der vierte. Aber: der erste, der dritte, der siebte.“
findings.problem: This round-1 finding is not fixed. The fix removed the only 8th from the Sp2 model turns but left the card unchanged. The card's rule still generates ✗„achtte“ (acht + -te) and ✗„am achtten“, because „der achte“ is missing from the exceptions. The card is the level's only ordinal card: u12 reuses the dates, and the LS2 generator numbers.dictation (datum-tag-monat) can draw the 8th. A simplification on a rule card that has become false is exactly what §9.5 asks reviewers to catch.
findings.fix: de: „… Aber: der erste, der dritte, der siebte, der achte. …“ (47 → 49 words; the a1.2 limit is 60). Add the table row ["8.", "der achte", "am achten"]. en: „irregular: erste, dritte, siebte, achte“.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-05 fixture: a card for g.ordinalzahlen-datum must list every ordinal from 1 to 19 that does not follow cardinal + -te (erste, dritte, siebte/siebente, achte). Test by deriving 1.–19. from the card's stated rule and comparing the result with the correct forms.

findings.quote: r05 „Arjun hat keinen Ausweis. Er bringt seinen ___ mit.“ accepted [Pass] · r01 „Das ist nicht der Pass. Das ist nur eine ___ vom Pass.“ accepted [Kopie]
findings.problem: „Er bringt seinen Reisepass mit.“ and „eine Fotokopie vom Pass“ are correct and natural. Reisepass is the everyday full word, and it is what the document says on its cover. The real checker grades both as WRONG (checkAnswer → result "wrong"; Levenshtein > 1). These are defensible second answers that are not accepted, which the rubric rates MAJOR. Both items sit in the plateau, mehr-ueben and repair banks, so they are graded outside the unit as well.
findings.fix: r05: accepted [Pass, Reisepass], acceptedWhy {"Reisepass": "auch richtig: der Reisepass = der Pass"}. r01: accepted [Kopie, Fotokopie], acceptedWhy {"Fotokopie": "auch richtig: die Fotokopie = die Kopie"}.
findings.proposedRule: Lexicon entries get an optional alsoAccept list of common full forms (Pass → Reisepass, Kopie → Fotokopie, Ausweis → Personalausweis). ITM-10 then requires a fill_blank keyed on such a lemma to list them in accepted[], or to exclude them explicitly in promptDe.

Perception: the four listen_select items now carry their punctuation in the quote, so the played Computerstimme matches the key („?“ ↔ Frage). The quote is masked until the item is answered, so the punctuation gives nothing away.
Facts: f01–f04 are verified, with a fresh check date and correct exceptions. The Fokus says only what f01/f02 support, plus neutral advice (pünktlich, Ausweis mit Foto, zum Beispiel Pass).
